items.q: Aschoff bodies with caterpillar chromatin macrophages indicate which disease?
items.exp: Aschoff bodies are the pathognomonic granulomatous foci of rheumatic carditis containing Anitschkov cells with caterpillar chromatin. They appear weeks after streptococcal pharyngitis.
r: Incorrect. Endocarditis shows infected destructive vegetations.
Correct. Aschoff bodies define rheumatic carditis.
Incorrect. Libman Sacks gives sterile verrucous lupus vegetations.
Incorrect. Carcinoid causes right sided fibrous plaques.
items.kp: Caterpillar macrophages in heart mean rheumatic carditis.

items.q: Chronic rheumatic disease most characteristically narrows which valve into a fish mouth?
items.exp: The mitral valve bears the brunt of rheumatic scarring with commissural fusion and chordal shortening producing fish mouth stenosis. Aortic involvement usually accompanies mitral disease.
r: Incorrect. Aortic disease rarely occurs alone rheumatically.
Correct. Mitral stenosis is the rheumatic signature.
Incorrect. Tricuspid rheumatic disease is uncommon.
Incorrect. Pulmonary valve is almost never rheumatic.
items.kp: Rheumatic heart disease speaks first through the mitral valve.

items.q: Which organism causes acute destructive endocarditis even on previously normal valves?
items.exp: Staphylococcus aureus is virulent enough to infect normal valves and destroy them rapidly with metastatic abscesses. Viridans streptococci cause subacute disease on previously damaged valves.
r: Incorrect. Viridans causes subacute disease on damaged valves.
Correct. Staph aureus attacks normal valves acutely.
Incorrect. Enterococcus is subacute, often genitourinary sourced.
Incorrect. Coxiella causes chronic culture negative disease.
items.kp: Acute plus normal valve equals staph aureus until proven otherwise.

items.q: Painful Osler nodes versus painless Janeway lesions: Janeway lesions represent what?
o: Septic microemboli to palms and soles
items.exp: Janeway lesions are painless haemorrhagic macules from septic emboli, while Osler nodes are painful immune mediated nodules. Both support endocarditis but by different mechanisms.
r: Incorrect. Immune complexes explain Osler nodes instead.
Correct. Janeway lesions are septic microemboli.
Incorrect. Splinters sit under nails non specifically.
Incorrect. Roth spots are retinal haemorrhages with pale centres.
items.kp: Painful is immune (Osler); painless is embolic (Janeway).

items.q: Culture negative endocarditis with chronic course should prompt testing for which organism classically?
items.exp: Coxiella burnetii causes chronic culture negative endocarditis diagnosed serologically, part of the HACEK and zoonotic workup when cultures stay sterile. Prior antibiotics are the commonest overall cause.
r: Incorrect. Epidermidis grows in cultures on prosthetic material.
Correct. Coxiella is the classic serology diagnosed cause.
Incorrect. Fungi usually affect prosthetic valves and immunocompromised hosts with positive clues.
Incorrect. Pneumococcus grows readily and presents acutely.
items.kp: Chronic plus sterile cultures: think Coxiella serology.

items.q: Libman Sacks vegetations occur in which condition on both valve surfaces?
items.exp: Libman Sacks endocarditis produces small sterile verrucous vegetations on either surface of mitral and aortic valves in lupus, associated with antiphospholipid antibodies and embolism risk.
r: Incorrect. Rheumatic vegetations line closure edges acutely.
Correct. Lupus causes Libman Sacks vegetations.
Incorrect. Infective vegetations contain organisms and destroy tissue.
Incorrect. Carcinoid deposits fibrous plaques on right sided valves.
items.kp: Sterile both surface vegetations in lupus: Libman Sacks.

items.q: Bicuspid aortic valve predisposes to which earlier complication?
o: Calcific aortic stenosis at younger age plus aortopathy
items.exp: Bicuspid valves experience abnormal stress, calcifying one to two decades earlier, and associate with ascending aortic dilation and dissection risk needing surveillance.
r: Incorrect. Mitral disease is rheumatic, not bicuspid linked.
Correct. Early calcific stenosis plus aortopathy.
Incorrect. Right sided lesions do not follow bicuspid aortic valves.
Incorrect. Pulmonary stenosis is a separate congenital lesion.
items.kp: Bicuspid means earlier stenosis and a watched aorta.

items.q: Carcinoid heart disease affects mainly which valves and why?
o: Right sided, lung monoamine oxidase inactivates serotonin before left heart
items.exp: Gut carcinoid serotonin reaches right heart via venous return causing fibrous tricuspid and pulmonary plaques, while pulmonary enzymes clear it before the left heart unless a shunt or lung tumour exists.
r: Incorrect. The lungs protect the left heart by clearing serotonin.
Correct. Right sided disease because lungs inactivate serotonin.
Incorrect. Left valves are characteristically spared.
Incorrect. Tricuspid and pulmonary valves bear the disease.
items.kp: Carcinoid spares the left heart thanks to lung enzymes.

items.q: Jones criteria are used to diagnose what?
items.exp: Jones criteria combine major manifestations (carditis, arthritis, chorea, erythema marginatum, nodules) with minor features and streptococcal evidence to diagnose acute rheumatic fever. Duke criteria serve endocarditis instead.
r: Incorrect. Duke criteria diagnose endocarditis.
Correct. Jones criteria diagnose rheumatic fever.
Incorrect. Severity uses echocardiographic gradients and areas.
Incorrect. Prosthetic failure needs imaging and cultures.
items.kp: Jones for rheumatic fever; Duke for endocarditis. Keep them apart.

items.q: Mitral stenosis most dangerously promotes which rhythm and complication pairing?
o: Atrial fibrillation with left atrial thrombus embolism
items.exp: Stretched fibrillating left atria in mitral stenosis stagnate blood into thrombus that embolises systemically, especially to brain. Rate control and anticoagulation decisions follow this risk.
r: Incorrect. Ventricular arrhythmia follows ventricular scar instead.
Correct. AF plus atrial thrombus embolism.
Incorrect. Block follows conduction system disease or inferior infarction.
Incorrect. Accessory pathways are congenital, unrelated.
items.kp: Stenotic mitral plus fibrillation equals clot risk. Anticoagulate by protocol.
